name: Banana and skim milk diet

card.summary: A 1930s-era fad diet built around bananas and skim milk, used by people aiming to lose weight and look leaner.
card.note: Single-food-style diets are described by dietetic bodies as nutritionally restrictive.

quick.overview:
The banana and skim milk diet is a food-specific fad diet from the 1930s that centres meals on bananas and skim (fat-free) milk. People used this kind of plan to cut calories and lose weight, which is how it connects to looks: a leaner body and face.
Wikipedia lists it among food-specific diets alongside better-known ones such as the grapefruit and morning banana diets. Few detailed sources describe its original rules, and no clinical trials of this particular diet were found.
quick.how: In general terms, plans of this type limit eating to a few foods for a set period. Specific rules for this diet are not documented.
quick.risks: The American Heart Association advises avoiding highly restrictive fad diets, and the British Dietetic Association recommends consulting a dietitian before starting any diet. Reviews of fad diets note that lost weight is often regained.

lead: The banana and skim milk diet is a 1930s fad diet in which bananas and skim milk make up most of what is eaten. It is listed in Wikipedia's fad diet navigation under food-specific diets, which encourage large amounts of a single food or a very short list of foods.[1]

People use diets of this kind to reduce calorie intake and lose body fat, which changes overall appearance, including facial leanness. The 1930s also saw other food-specific plans such as the grapefruit "Hollywood" diet and an early liquid protein product.[1]
Dietary bodies describe restrictive plans as tending to be nutritionally unsound if followed beyond a few days, and note that short-term weight loss is often regained.[1]

angle.text: Proponents of food-specific diets present them as a simple route to losing weight. This diet has little modern documentation beyond its listing among historical fad diets.

paras: Wikipedia's overview of fad diets groups plans that encourage large amounts of a single food, with the cabbage soup diet as its example, and lists the banana and skim milk diet and the morning banana diet in its navigation of such diets.[1]

The same overview states that restrictive approaches tend to be nutritionally unsound and can cause serious health problems if followed for more than a few days, that the American Heart Association advises avoiding highly restrictive fad diets, and that the British Dietetic Association recommends consulting a dietitian before starting any diet.[1]

Posts on T Nation mention bananas and milk as ordinary parts of bulking meals, for example porridge, a banana and a pint of milk before a rugby match, which is a different use from a banana-and-skim-milk weight-loss plan.[2]

timeline.event: Banana and skim milk diet appears as a fad diet.[1]
